verdict.root_cause: Checkout is the caller that noticed, not the fault. Traces localise the degradation to one hop: checkout -> cart on EmptyCart, which carries error status and whose cart-side self time accounts for essentially the whole trace duration [tr_1a9b167675c0]. The span errors blame cart's Redis/Valkey cart-storage backend as unreachable, yet in the same traces cart's GetCart and its HGET against that same store complete sub-millisecond with no error [tr_1a9b167675c0] — the store is plainly reachable, so the failure is produced by one code path inside cart rather than by the datastore or the network. Checkout's error ratio is intermittent and bursty (mean ~2%, peak ~9.5%, returning to zero, no sustained step) [tr_29bcd17fe3ee, tr_dedc20b347cf], consistent with only EmptyCart-bearing requests failing. No deploy, config edit, dependency bump or flag record appears in the change log [tr_e4d55aea9617, tr_eb7f7d2fbe37]. An operation-scoped failure with no artifact or config change recorded fits a runtime flag in the flag store having enabled a failing EmptyCart path in cart.
verdict.reasoning: Traces rule out payment, shipping, currency, product-catalog and email, rule out a broad shared-resource slowdown (siblings including flagd resolution inside cart stay fast), and rule out checkout's own logic (≈1ms self time in multi-second traces) [tr_1a9b167675c0]. That leaves cart. Within cart, the discriminator is that one operation errors claiming the store is unreachable while another operation reads that same store successfully in the same traces [tr_1a9b167675c0] — which excludes process_freeze and network_partition (cart serves other traffic), datastore_corruption (reads succeed, no decode failures) and disk_fill. The intermittent, non-sustained error shape [tr_29bcd17fe3ee, tr_dedc20b347cf] argues against exhaustion. The empty change log [tr_e4d55aea9617, tr_eb7f7d2fbe37] is what a flag-store flip looks like, though it is weak: it covered checkout only and its window ran forward from onset, not before it [tr_e4d55aea9617]. Checkout and frontend logs returned zero lines of any severity and contribute nothing either way [tr_01acf7765d81, tr_d5ee36bf7938].
open_questions: No dispatch touched cart directly — its logs, metrics and change/flag history were never queried, so the flag is inferred, never observed.
The change-log window ran forward from 22:32:31 rather than before it, so no pre-incident change for any service was actually sampled.
Total log silence for both checkout and frontend is unexplained; if it is a real outage rather than a collection gap, the picture changes materially.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart's connection path to its Redis/Valkey store is genuinely broken for the EmptyCart write path, so cart waits and fails on that call.
alternatives.why_not: Successful sub-millisecond HGET reads against the same store in the same traces make a real connectivity or slowness problem hard to sustain [tr_1a9b167675c0].

alternatives.root_cause: A configuration value in cart names a wrong address or credential for the cart-storage backend on the write path.
alternatives.why_not: No config change was recorded and cart reaches the same store successfully for reads, so a wrong address or credential would have to be path-specific — possible but less economical than a flagged code path.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The observable that would justify a later proposal is a change-history record for cart naming a flag or config mutation at or before 2026-10-08T22:02:31Z, plus cart-side logs or span events on the EmptyCart path that show the failing branch being taken. Neither exists on this board: the only change queries run were against checkout [tr_e4d55aea9617, tr_eb7f7d2fbe37], both returned empty, and both ran forward from 22:32:31 so they did not even sample the pre-incident period.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a change-history query against cart, over a window ending at 2026-10-08T22:02:31Z, returns a prior configuration or flag record for cart inside the incident window. That single result would satisfy both preconditions of revert_config and make a config_revert on cart proposable. It is also wrong if cart's own logs show the EmptyCart failure beginning at a timestamp that coincides with a recorded flag flip. Until cart is queried directly, the flag is an inference from the shape of the failure (operation-scoped, intermittent, no artifact change) and not an observation — the verdict says so itself and rates its own confidence low.
proposal.risk: The risk of acting here, not of abstaining. revert_config on cart would recreate cart's container with a configuration nobody has read, chosen on the strength of a flag nobody has seen. If the real mechanism is something else — a cart-side connection-pool leak or a stuck client against cart-storage, which the traces are equally consistent with given GetCart/HGET succeed sub-millisecond on the same store [tr_1a9b167675c0] — the revert would restore a config that is not the problem and the recreate would mask it by resetting process state, destroying the evidence and producing a false confirmation. A wrong config value for a dependency address would move cart's traffic somewhere unintended. The risk of abstaining is that an intermittent ~2% checkout error ratio persists; that is tolerable for the time it takes to query cart.
proposal.blast_radius: Had an action been taken on cart: cart itself, plus checkout and frontend, which reach cart on this path, and frontend-proxy behind frontend — all four would see connection resets for the duration of the recreate. Checkout's error ratio would spike above its current ~9.5% peak [tr_29bcd17fe3ee] during that interval. Abstaining changes nothing and is visible to no one; the cost is only the continued intermittent failures already present.
proposal._note: Also relevant: no permitted action targets the flag store itself, which is where the hypothesised fault lives. revert_config acts on a service's own config, and cart is the consumer of the flag, not its owner. Even with a cart change record in hand, the right fix may be outside what this system can do.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on checkout with no open incidents to attribute it to cannot be dismissed. Single seed with many unmeasured downstream dependencies gives no clear fault signature yet.
